# The proposal
<!--
How are you going to solve the problem? Include the concrete actions you
will take and an estimated timeline. What are likely failure modes and
how will you recover from them?

This is where the proposal should be outlined.
-->

This proposal is to fund the completion of the R package, {geoarrowrs}, which is a geoarrow-native compute engine for the R ecosystem.

The R package will provide memory efficient and parallelized implementation for geometric operations out of the box.
In addition, it will provide advanced spatial join and query operations.
The R package will integrate into the existing ecosystem with a focus on integration with {arrow}, {dplyr}, and {sf} to minimize friction in adoption.

This proposal is for work in the following

1. Core geometry algorithm implementation
2. Parallelization and
3. {sf} integration


## Overview
<!--
At a high-level address what your proposal is and how it will address
the problem identified. Highlight any benefits to the R Community that
follow from solving the problem. This should be your most compelling
section.

Include concrete actions you will take and estimated timeline.
-->


The {geoarrowrs} package is a GeoArrow-native spatial computation engine designed for ergonomic use within the R ecosystem. The package is in the middle of its development life cycle and this grant would fund its completion.

This package aims to be faster than geos, competitive with duckspatial and sedonadb, and as ergonomic as {sf} (with a drop in replacement via `mask_sf()`) for **in memory** computation.

Today, the package provides:

- performant readers for shapfile, GeoJson, and FlatGeobuf
- R-tree and KD-tree spatial indexes
- Spatial, nearest neighbor, and distance band joins
- User defined functions registered with {arrow}

Completion of the package is split into four milestones:

1. Complete core geometry engine so that every algorithm provided by the Rust crate [`geo`](https://github.com/georust/geo) as of this writing is available from R. This would achieve near parity with {sf} on most operations.
2. Create spatial indexes that can be written to disk which can be used to spatiall sort geometries for more efficient GeoParquet storage.
3. Provide drop in {sf} compatibility via `mask_sf()` so that {geoarrowrs} can be used as a backend for {sf} and release the package on CRAN.
4. Persist coordinate reference systems, so that GeoArrow transfer between R, Python, DuckDB, and GDAL can be lossless. This milestone also targets GeoParquet column meta persistence enabled by milestone 2.




## Prior art

The {geoarrowrs} package is the culmination of years of exploring the intersection of Rust, geospatial, and GeoArrow.
Initially, the [{rsgeo}](https://github.com/JosiahParry/rsgeo) package was created to be a zero-dependency and high-performance spatial computation engine with [Rust based conversion](https://github.com/JosiahParry/sfconversions) to and from {sf}.

During this time GeoArrow began to pick up. With the [{anime}](https://github.com/JosiahParry/anime/) line matching algorithm being a proof of concept for use of GeoArrow in R built on my [arrow-extendr](https://github.com/extendr/arrow-extendr) Rust library which provides FFI between R and Rust for {arrow}, {nanoarrow}, {polars}, and {geoarrow} packages.


In 2024, the [initial version](https://github.com/JosiahParry/geoarrowrs/tree/archive/pre-rewrite) of this package was started. But development was paused due to an unstable geoarrow-rust API, and challenges with Arrow FFI that ar now resolved.

### Architecture

<!--
What does the high-level architecture look like?
-->

- Rust based R package via [extendr](https://github.com/extendr/extendr)
- Arrow FFI between R and Rust via [arrow-extendr](https://github.com/extendr/arrow-extendr)
- GeoArrow array representation via [geoarrow-rs](https://geoarrow.org/geoarrow-rs/)
- Native algorithms using [geo](https://github.com/georust/geo)
- Coordinate reference systems via [projjson](https://github.com/JosiahParry/projjson-rs)
- Spatial Indexing using geo-index
- Readers and writer using:
    - geozero https://docs.rs/crate/geozero/0.14.0
    - geojson
    - flatgeobuf
- Parallelism via https://docs.rs/rayon
